# QuantumVault Architecture & Distributed Specification

## Overview
QuantumVault is a multi-tenant, high-throughput secure document indexing and distributed retrieval engine. It is designed for low-latency question answering over encrypted knowledge bases with strict provenance guarantees.

## Consensus and Cluster Topology
QuantumVault clusters operate using a Raft-based consensus protocol. The cluster configuration mandates a 150ms heartbeat interval between the leader and follower nodes, and a 300ms election timeout to detect leader partition or node failure. Cluster membership changes require a two-phase joint consensus transition.

## Data Encryption and Key Management
All data chunks and metadata are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption. Encryption keys are generated via a hardware security module (HSM) and are rotated automatically every 90 days. In-transit communication across internal microservices requires mutual TLS (mTLS 1.3) with elliptic curve cryptography (X25519).

## Hybrid Retrieval Architecture
The hybrid retrieval engine combines dense vector search with sparse lexical search to achieve optimal recall and precision:
1. Dense Retrieval: Chunks are converted into 384-dimensional dense vectors using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings and queried in ChromaDB using HNSW cosine distance indexing.
2. Sparse Retrieval: An in-memory BM25Okapi index scores exact token matches against session-scoped corpora.
3. Fusion: Results from dense and sparse retrieval paths are fused using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with a ranking constant k=60.
4. Reranking: The top 20 candidate passages from RRF are reranked using the cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 cross-encoder running in a dedicated thread pool to keep the asynchronous event loop non-blocking.

## Smart Caching Tier
The caching tier is backed by Redis with a default time-to-live (TTL) of 3600 seconds (1 hour). Cache keys are formatted as `cache:{session_id}:v{corpus_version}:{sha256(rewritten_query)}`. The corpus version increments monotonically whenever a new document is ingested, automatically invalidating stale cached answers. Exact cache hits bypass retrieval and LLM generation, returning responses in under 50 milliseconds.

## Contextual Query Rewriting
Multi-turn conversations use anaphora resolution powered by llama-3.1-8b-instant. Ambiguous follow-up questions containing pronouns such as "it", "they", or "those" are rewritten into standalone search queries before retrieval is executed.
